messages:
kevin: Morning - seeing a cluster of GPU attach failures in eu-west3 around 04:10 UTC. Symptoms point to long nvme fsync pauses during janitor scrub windows, followed by occasional controller resets.

oshana: Sample logs? can you paste a snippet?

kevin: from eu-west3-cn-211: 
[04:12] nvme0n1: io timeout, resetting controller
[04:12] EXT4-fs: delayed allocate failed for ino=98765
[04:12] janitor: shard=17 start

li: iostat shows huge wkB/s with high await - looks like metadata fsync bursts from the janitor. If a drive hits a firmware corner case during heavy fsyncs it can reset.

storage-bot: alert: nvme_journal_stall detected, hosts_affected=12 region=eu-west3 window=30m severity=high

oshana: Quick mitigations: 1) reduce janitor concurrency in eu-west3 (8->4) 2) add per-shard fsync cap (e.g., 64KB/s) 3) stagger shard starts by random(0..300s)

li: And add an attach fallback: on device-reset/timeout, mark node transient-unhealthy for 30s and retry attach to alternative candidates in same AZ up to 3 times. Emits metrics: attach.fallback.attempts/success.

kevin: agree. lowering concurrency will increase total janitor time but reduces peak fsync pressure. rough estimate: +4h run time for eu-west3, cost << $200/day.

oshana: I'll flip the janitor concurrency and add stagger now. storage-bot will post config change.

storage-bot: action: janitor_concurrency_change applied region=eu-west3 old=8 new=4 by=oshana

li: I'll open PR for attach fallback and metrics, gate by region flag, canary in eu-west3.

kevin: I'll file vendor bug with nvme logs, SMART/thermal dumps, and host list. If resets persist after throttling we consider isolating hosts.

oshana: Status update in 30m. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
